_note: Curated core list. One row per SOC 2020 unit group. Numbers live in the per-source snapshots, not here. DEMO SNAPSHOT: SOC mappings and every figure must be checked by a person against the linked source before real use.

occupations.title: Software developer
occupations.summary: Designs, writes and tests the software behind apps, websites and systems.
occupations.first_step: Finish one small project on a free platform (for example a CS50 or freeCodeCamp exercise) and put it on GitHub.

occupations.title: Cyber security specialist
occupations.summary: Protects organisations from hacking, fraud and data loss, and investigates attacks.
occupations.first_step: Sign up for CyberFirst or a free capture-the-flag challenge for school pupils.

occupations.title: Data scientist or statistician
occupations.summary: Turns large sets of data into findings that help organisations decide.
occupations.first_step: Pick an open dataset (for example from the Office for National Statistics) and make three charts that answer one question.

occupations.title: IT support technician
occupations.summary: Keeps computers, networks and accounts working, and helps people fix problems.
occupations.first_step: Offer to help your school's IT team for one lunchtime a week, and note what problems come up.

occupations.title: Mechanical engineer
occupations.summary: Designs and improves machines, from engines to medical devices to wind turbines.
occupations.study_level: Degree (BEng or MEng) or degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Join or start an Arkwright, F1 in Schools or similar engineering challenge.

occupations.title: Civil engineer
occupations.summary: Plans and builds roads, bridges, flood defences and water systems.
occupations.study_level: Degree (BEng or MEng) or degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Ask a local construction or engineering firm about a work-experience day.

occupations.title: Electrical engineer
occupations.summary: Designs power systems, from the national grid to electric vehicles and renewables.
occupations.study_level: Degree (BEng or MEng) or degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Build a simple circuit project with a starter kit and write down what you learned.

occupations.title: Electrician
occupations.summary: Installs and repairs wiring, solar panels, EV chargers and building electrics.
occupations.first_step: Look up apprenticeship open days at your nearest college and book one.

occupations.title: Plumber and heating engineer
occupations.soc_title: Plumbers and heating and ventilating installers and repairers
occupations.summary: Fits and maintains water, heating and heat-pump systems in homes and buildings.
occupations.first_step: Ask a local heating installer if you can shadow them for a day.

occupations.title: Carpenter and joiner
occupations.summary: Makes and fits wooden structures, from roof frames to staircases and furniture.
occupations.first_step: Make one finished piece in your school workshop and photograph each stage.

occupations.title: Bricklayer
occupations.summary: Builds and repairs walls, homes and other structures with brick and block.
occupations.first_step: Find a 'have a go' construction taster session at a local college.

occupations.title: Vehicle technician
occupations.summary: Diagnoses and repairs cars and vans, including electric and hybrid vehicles.
occupations.first_step: Ask a local garage about a Saturday job or a week of work experience.

occupations.title: Community nurse
occupations.summary: Cares for patients in their homes and in the community, often with long-term conditions.
occupations.study_level: Nursing degree or nursing degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Volunteer with a local care home, hospice or the NHS volunteer responders.

occupations.title: Mental health nurse
occupations.summary: Supports people with mental illness to recover and manage their health.
occupations.study_level: Nursing degree or nursing degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Complete a free online mental health awareness course and volunteer with a youth or peer-support group.

occupations.title: Physiotherapist
occupations.summary: Helps people recover movement after injury, illness or surgery.
occupations.first_step: Ask a local physiotherapy clinic or sports club physio if you can shadow them.

occupations.title: Occupational therapist
occupations.summary: Helps people with illness or disability do everyday tasks and live independently.
occupations.first_step: Read the Royal College of Occupational Therapists careers pages and email one local OT team.

occupations.title: Speech and language therapist
occupations.summary: Helps children and adults with communication, speech and swallowing difficulties.
occupations.first_step: Volunteer with a reading or homework club for younger children.

occupations.title: Paramedic
occupations.summary: Responds to emergencies and treats patients at the scene and on the way to hospital.
occupations.first_step: Join St John Ambulance or British Red Cross youth first-aid training.

occupations.title: Pharmacist
occupations.summary: Makes sure medicines are safe and right for each patient, and advises on health.
occupations.study_level: Master of Pharmacy (4 years) plus a training year
occupations.first_step: Ask your local pharmacy about a week of work experience.

occupations.title: Radiographer
occupations.summary: Uses X-ray, MRI and other imaging to diagnose, or radiation to treat cancer.
occupations.first_step: Look up a hospital radiography open day and ask to visit the imaging department.

occupations.title: Care worker
occupations.summary: Supports older and disabled people with daily living at home or in care homes.
occupations.study_level: No formal entry requirement; Level 2–3 qualifications on the job
occupations.first_step: Volunteer a few hours a week at a care home or with a befriending charity.

occupations.title: Secondary school teacher
occupations.summary: Teaches a subject to pupils aged 11 to 18 and supports their progress.
occupations.study_level: Degree plus a teaching qualification (PGDE or PGCE)
occupations.first_step: Offer to help as a paired-reading or maths mentor for younger pupils.

occupations.title: Primary school teacher
occupations.summary: Teaches children aged 4 to 11 across all subjects.
occupations.first_step: Ask a local primary school or Brownies/Cubs group if you can help out.

occupations.title: Social worker
occupations.summary: Supports children, families and adults through difficult times and keeps them safe.
occupations.study_level: Social work degree or degree apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Volunteer with a youth club, food bank or young carers' service.

occupations.title: Clinical psychologist
occupations.summary: Assesses and treats people with mental and emotional difficulties using talking therapies.
occupations.study_level: Psychology degree, then a doctorate (usually 6+ years in total)
occupations.first_step: Read one accessible psychology book and volunteer for a listening or peer-support service.

occupations.title: Accountant
occupations.summary: Manages money, tax and financial records for businesses and people.
occupations.first_step: Apply for a school-leaver insight day with an accountancy firm (many run them online).

occupations.title: Solicitor
occupations.summary: Advises clients on the law and represents them in deals and disputes.
occupations.study_level: Law degree (LLB in Scotland) or solicitor apprenticeship in England
occupations.first_step: Join your school debating club or a mock trial competition.

occupations.title: Architect
occupations.summary: Designs buildings and spaces that are safe, useful and good to be in.
occupations.first_step: Start a sketchbook of buildings you like and why, and book an architecture open day.

occupations.title: Graphic and multimedia designer
occupations.summary: Creates visual designs for brands, websites, games and print.
occupations.study_level: College course, degree or Level 3–4 apprenticeship
occupations.first_step: Design three posters for a real school event and add them to an online portfolio.

occupations.title: Quantity surveyor
occupations.summary: Manages the costs and contracts of building projects from start to finish.
occupations.first_step: Look up the RICS careers site and ask a local construction firm about a site visit.

occupations.title: Environmental scientist
occupations.summary: Studies and protects air, water, land and wildlife, and advises on climate and pollution.
occupations.first_step: Join a local conservation volunteering day or a citizen-science survey.

occupations.title: Chef
occupations.summary: Plans menus and cooks food in restaurants, hotels, schools and hospitals.
occupations.first_step: Get a weekend kitchen job or volunteer to cook for a community event.

occupations.title: Biomedical scientist
occupations.summary: Tests samples in laboratories to help diagnose and treat disease.
occupations.first_step: Enter a school science competition or join a science club project.

occupations.title: Vet
occupations.summary: Diagnoses and treats illness and injury in pets, farm animals and wildlife.
occupations.first_step: Arrange work experience at a vet practice, farm or animal shelter (vet schools expect it).

occupations.title: Police officer
occupations.summary: Keeps communities safe, responds to incidents and investigates crime.
occupations.study_level: Degree, degree apprenticeship or direct entry (varies by force)
occupations.first_step: Join your local Police Cadets or Volunteer Police Cadets group.

occupations.title: Investment analyst
occupations.soc_title: Finance and investment analysts and advisers
occupations.summary: Researches companies and markets, and advises on where money should be invested and at what risk.
occupations.first_step: Follow three listed companies for a month in a spreadsheet and write one paragraph on what moved each price.

occupations.title: Project manager
occupations.soc_title: Business and financial project management professionals
occupations.summary: Plans and leads projects so they finish on time and on budget, from IT systems to new offices.
occupations.first_step: Run one real project end to end, like a school event or fundraiser, and keep a simple plan, budget and risk list.

occupations.title: Sales and business development manager
occupations.soc_title: Sales accounts and business development managers
occupations.summary: Finds new customers, builds relationships with them and wins deals for a business.
occupations.study_level: No fixed route; Level 4–6 apprenticeship or degree common
occupations.first_step: Get a weekend sales or customer-facing job and note which conversations led to a sale.

occupations.title: Marketing executive
occupations.summary: Plans campaigns that get products and causes noticed, online and off.
occupations.first_step: Run the social media for a school club or local charity for a month and track what gets the most response.

occupations.title: Construction manager
occupations.soc_title: Production managers and directors in construction
occupations.summary: Runs building projects on site: people, safety, schedule and cost.
occupations.study_level: Degree or degree apprenticeship, or up from a trade
occupations.first_step: Ask a local builder or housing developer if you can shadow a site manager for a day.
